root_cause.text: The IPv6 FIB route insertion logic in `fib6_add_rt2node()` cleared `RTF_ADDRCONF` on an existing route even when that route had a gateway, which incorrectly made it ECMP-eligible without adding it to `fib6_siblings`, causing sibling-count inconsistencies and a later `BUG_ON()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the condition in `net/ipv6/ip6_fib.c` to clear `RTF_ADDRCONF` only when `!iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family`, and the commit message explains that routes with a gateway “become eligible for ECMP” after clearing `RTF_ADDRCONF` but “were never added to the fib6_siblings list,” leading to a mismatch that triggers `BUG_ON(sibling->fib6_nsiblings != rt->fib6_nsiblings)`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid clearing addrconf and prefix route flags for routes that have a nexthop gateway family set.
intent_record.what: The condition guarding the clearing of RTF_ADDRCONF and RTF_PREFIX_RT was expanded: it now only clears those flags when the incoming route does not have RTF_ADDRCONF or RTF_PREFIX_RT set and the existing iterator nexthop gateway family is zero (`!iter->fib6_nh->fib_nh_gw_family`).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code will preserve the addrconf/prefix route flags for entries whose nexthop has a gateway family, instead of unconditionally clearing them whenever the new route lacks those flags. This changes which IPv6 route entries retain those metadata flags during insertion/update.

grouping_result.intent: Avoid clearing addrconf and prefix route flags for routes that have a nexthop gateway family set.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it prevents clearing addrconf/prefix flags on routes with a gateway/nexthop, which was the condition that incorrectly made the route ECMP-eligible without sibling tracking and led to the BUG_ON().

candidates.rationale: This is the direct operation that clears RTF_ADDRCONF on an existing route. Per the root cause, clearing this flag on a route that has a gateway incorrectly makes it ECMP-eligible without properly adding it to fib6_siblings, leading to sibling-count inconsistency and a later BUG_ON().

vuln_statements.explanation: This line clears RTF_ADDRCONF on an existing IPv6 route. Per the root cause, doing so for routes that already have a gateway incorrectly makes the route ECMP-eligible without adding it to fib6_siblings, which later causes sibling-count inconsistency and a BUG_ON().
